maestro-world-gospel-30-v1-25:
[Verse 1]
The city folds its daylight like a coat upon the chair
One more train goes rumbling through the cold November air
I used to count the windows where the yellow lamplights shone
And wonder if a dream could be a place to call my own
My notebooks filled with melodies I never let them hear
I kept my voice behind a door I locked because of fear
Tonight I take that little key, I turn it in my hand
The quiet in my chest becomes a rhythm I can stand

[Pre-Chorus]
Every light along this street is somebody's beginning
I can hear my heartbeat change, I can feel the night is listening

[Chorus]
Moscow midnight, carry me home
Not to the life I knew, but the life I'll make my own
Moscow midnight, let the windows glow
I've been waiting for a sign, now I'm learning how to go
I don't need the whole world to hear me tonight
One honest little song is enough to strike the light
Moscow midnight, the road is wide
I'm walking toward tomorrow with my music at my side

[Verse 2]
The baker shuts the shutters and the buses shake the snow
A woman hums a lullaby to someone down below
I send my sister one short note: “The band begins on Friday”
She sends a row of rising suns and says she's coming my way
The sidewalk is a silver line, the air is sharp and clear
The song inside the notebook finally sounds like something here
A promise doesn't need a crowd, a trumpet or a drum
It only needs one person brave enough to say, “I'll come”

[Bridge]
If the morning finds me frightened, I'll remember how I chose
A room with just one microphone and a window full of snow
Let the notes fall imperfect; let the people see me try
You don't have to own the heavens just to sing beneath the sky

[Final Chorus]
Moscow midnight, carry me home
Not to the life I knew, but the life I'll make my own
Moscow midnight, let the windows glow
I've been waiting for a sign, now I'm learning how to go
One honest little song is enough to strike the light
Moscow midnight, I'm ready for the morning light

[Outro]
The last train leaves the station, but my song is here to stay
And the city keeps its promise as the dark becomes the day.
maestro-world-gospel-30-v1-16:
[Verso 1]
Traigo polvo del camino en las costuras del pantalón
Una foto de la casa y una carta en el cajón
Hace tiempo dije cosas que no supe remediar
Me fui buscando respuestas y olvidé cómo escuchar
Hoy la sierra se levanta con su sombra sobre el sol
Y mi pecho va ensayando las palabras del perdón
No vengo con mil promesas ni una historia que vender
Vengo solo con mis manos y las ganas de aprender

[Pre-Coro]
Cruza el aire una campana desde el pueblo hasta el palmar
Cada paso me recuerda lo que tengo que cambiar

[Coro]
Voy de regreso por el camino de ayer
Sin pedir que se me olvide lo que hice sin querer
Voy de regreso, no a ganar la discusión
Sino a tocar aquella puerta con respeto y corazón
Si me dejan, poco a poco, la confianza volverá
No se compra con palabras; con el tiempo se verá
Voy de regreso, y aunque tarde en comprender
El amor se cuida a diario, se demuestra al responder

[Verso 2]
La tienda sigue en la esquina, la banqueta sigue igual
La señora que nos conoce me saluda en el portal
Veo el árbol donde un día nos juramos no partir
Y recuerdo que escuchar también es una forma de vivir
En la mesa hay dos tazones y un silencio de verdad
No lo lleno con disculpas que pretendan apurar
Digo: “Sé que te hice daño, y no puedo deshacer
Cada noche que esperaste sin saber si iba a volver”

[Puente]
Si mañana no me abren, no buscaré otro culpable
Dejaré que mis acciones digan algo confiable
Voy a estar donde haga falta, sin exigir explicación
Porque a veces el regreso comienza con atención

[Coro Final]
Voy de regreso por el camino de ayer
Sin pedir que se me olvide lo que hice sin querer
Voy de regreso, con paciencia y con razón
A cuidar los días pequeños y a escuchar de corazón
Si me dejan, poco a poco, la confianza volverá
No se compra con palabras; con el tiempo se verá
Voy de regreso, y aunque tarde en comprender
El amor se cuida a diario y se aprende a sostener

[Salida]
La tarde cae sobre el cerro, se oye un perro en el solar
Dejo quietas mis maletas: hoy me toca conversar.
maestro-world-gospel-30-v1-28:
[Verse 1]
The kettle sings before the sun, the church doors open wide
Miss Evelyn brings the flowers, little James comes by her side
Some of us are full of laughter, some are carrying a weight
Some are coming straight from working through a long and lonely late
Yesterday was filled with questions we could barely speak aloud
But we're gathering together, every face a different cloud
There's a table in the fellowship hall, there's a place to set the bread
There's a voice that says, “We need you,” when a tired soul bows their head

[Pre-Chorus]
We don't have to hide the sorrow, we don't have to stand alone
There is work enough for kindness, there is room enough for hope

[Chorus — choir response]
This morning we will rise (we will rise)
With a promise in our eyes (in our eyes)
Take the mercy we've been given, make it living in the street
Put a little love in motion with our hands and with our feet
This morning we will stand (we will stand)
Lift a neighbor by the hand (by the hand)
Not because the road is easy, not because the sky is clear
But because the grace that found us has a place for everyone here

[Verse 2]
Brother Thomas has a toolbox, sister Ruth has soup to share
There's a young man in the back row who has finally found a chair
We can sing about tomorrow, but today is calling too
There are fences needing mending, there are things that we can do
So we'll listen to the lonely, we will check the elderly
We will bring a meal at dinnertime and help a family
Every hallelujah spoken finds its purpose when we leave
Let our living be the music that a weary heart receives

[Bridge — solo then choir]
If my faith is only thunder, let it soften into rain
If my prayer is only singing, let it ease another's pain
There is room beneath this ceiling for the hurting and the strong
And a whole wide world outside it where the morning song belongs

[Final Chorus — full choir]
This morning we will rise (we will rise)
With a promise in our eyes (in our eyes)
Take the mercy we've been given, make it living in the street
Put a little love in motion with our hands and with our feet
This morning we will stand (we will stand)
Lift a neighbor by the hand (by the hand)
Not because the road is easy, not because the sky is clear
But because the grace that found us has a place for everyone here

[Outro]
The last amen is spoken, but the promise isn't done
We carry Sunday morning into every day to come.
